references.text: Earlier in the chapter, the instruction is given to take a tribute for the Lord from the spoils of war—one part out of five hundred—which explains why 72 head of cattle were given to the Lord.
The principle of giving a portion of what was received to the Lord as a holy offering, just as the Levites were to give a tenth of the tithes they received.

Laws concerning tithes to the Lord from everything in the land, both from the produce of the soil and the fruit of trees and from the livestock, establishing the principle of giving a portion to the Lord.
The immediate context showing the distribution of the remaining spoils of war (sheep, donkeys) before the count of cattle in verse 38.
